title: Real log: rundll32 and comsvcs.dll
source: Real telemetry from OTRF Security-Datasets (MIT), lab-generated, not employer data
logs: 23:50:05 EventID=1 Host=WORKSTATION5 User=WORKSTATION5\wardog Image=C:\Windows\System32\rundll32.exe ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe CommandLine="rundll32.exe" C:\windows\System32\comsvcs.dll MiniDump 756 C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\lsass-comsvcs.dmp full
question: Explain what this command does and give your verdict.
explanation: comsvcs.dll MiniDump is a living-off-the-land way to dump process memory. PID 756 is almost certainly LSASS, and the dump goes to a Temp folder, so this is credential theft (T1003.001) with no extra tool dropped. Confirm the PID, find and secure the dump file, and look for it leaving the host.
